latest.title: Apoc-Air 0.2.0
latest.notes:
# Apoc-Air 0.2.0

Needs SigmaMod 2.0: the gyroplane is a Lua asset now.

## The gyroplane

- **A Lua asset**: `sigma_assets/apocagyro.lua` (9 KB) replaces `apocagyro.json` (108 KB). It is built from
  SigmaMod's parts library and makes the same gyroplane.
- **The flight controls are a library**: `sigma_assets/apocair/flight.lua` (`require "apocair.flight"`,
  `flight.controls(g, { input = ..., rotor = ... })`) holds the keys and mouse to the stick, pedals and throttle,
  the hand shove and the stabiliser. Another aircraft can use it as it is.
- **Parked means parked**: with nobody in the seat the wheel brakes are on. Before, getting out let go of them, and
  a gyroplane left on a slope rolled away.
- **The stabiliser is off with nobody aboard** (and when one spawns), so it doesn't work the rotor head of an empty
  aircraft. It comes back on when you sit down; V still switches it.
- The seat is where it belongs on every copy: SigmaMod 2.0 places an object made in the asset only once the object
  it is placed at exists.

## Install

Unzip into `Apocalypter/BepInEx/plugins`, replacing the `ApocAir` folder. Delete `ApocAir/sigma_assets/apocagyro.json`
if it is still there from 0.1.x (with both, the `.lua` wins, but the old file is dead weight).

# Apocapocket 2.0.10

Weapon recovery can now run after a puff while a joint is still lit. Version 2.0.9 protected the entire burn phase, which
skipped recovery in the reported case. The guard now distinguishes the lighting animation from ongoing smoking: both
smoking arms must already be hidden, the lighting FSM must be idle and burn progress must be valid before recovery is allowed.

Lighting and unfinished/unknown animation states stay protected. Native smoking continues to own burn progress, held Smoke
input, lights, consumption, discarded items and weed effects. Recovery does not replay End or reset the joint.
Extra-slot weapons and parked native hosts are preserved through the existing inventory transaction.

The watchdog also covers a selected weapon whose native hand handler remains inactive despite visible weapon prompts, and
honours the native re-equip delay when game time is slowed.

Recovery and state-snapshot messages require Debug/VerboseLog = true. Default logging stays quiet. If the issue persists,
enable that setting, restart and reproduce the puff/weapon draw, then remain in gameplay for at least 15 seconds and copy
BepInEx/LogOutput.log. Snapshots identify animation, hand, pause, menu, vehicle, save and transaction guards without clearing
another mod's pause or moving another mod's held object.

Replace the previous DLL with the included BepInEx/plugins/Apocapocket/Apocapocket.dll and restart. Keep only one plugin DLL.
Existing configuration, bindings and save format are retained.

Verified with 173 production-code checks and native Mono/Harmony checks. The affected player's reproduction still needs
validation; their prior log confirmed 2.0.9 loaded but did not capture the stalled weapon states.

latest.title: Apocasaver 2.0.4
latest.notes:
# Apocasaver 2.0.4

Fixes terrain-streaming hitches caused by repeatedly searching all loaded objects for missing location templates. Thanks to **@Wad67** for the profiling and [PR #1](https://github.com/DeonUrist/Apocasaver/pull/1), merged with the original contributor commit preserved.

The [follow-up fixes in PR #2](https://github.com/DeonUrist/Apocasaver/pull/2) reduce additional save and terrain work:

- Resolve templates from the actual pool prefab, keep same-name prefabs distinct, and reset template caches across scene/session changes.
- Reuse the terrain-history snapshot until history changes, while isolating writes made by load callbacks.
- Process only moved or deleted pool objects; skip empty movement batches.
- Check cleanup eligibility before building one reference index. Periodic cleanup scans stop while `CleanSaves` is disabled; enabling it starts fresh distance timing.
- Batch hand-pose metadata into the active save transaction or one delayed disk write. Failed delayed writes retain pending poses, and transactional reads see the latest cache.

Validation: release build with zero warnings/errors, **100 managed checks**, **78 isolated native Unity checks**, and **93 native checks with Apocapatrol 2.13.0 / Apocapocket 2.0.10** passed. Native fixtures cover pooling, history restoration, reference protection, metadata batching, real disk-lock retry and save rollback. They are constructed fixtures rather than a complete gameplay replay. [Verification details](https://github.com/DeonUrist/Apocasaver/blob/v2.0.4/docs/2.0.4-verification.md).

Extract `Apocasaver-2.0.4.zip` into the game directory, replacing `BepInEx/plugins/Apocasaver.dll`, then restart the game. Requires BepInEx 5; optional companion mods are packaged separately.

# Burner's Utilities 0.4.1

Needs SigmaMod 2.0: the items are Lua assets. Without SigmaMod, the items aren't there and everything else works.

## Trailer hitches

- **Hitches bolt on and hitch without Apocapocket.** The hitch switches its `Attach` and `HitchUse` FSMs on and off
  with the game's `EnableFSM`, whose default is to undo itself when its state is left: a frame later each FSM was back
  as it had been, so a loose hitch could end up with no Use prompt against a vehicle. Apocapocket switches a held
  item's `Attach` back on, which hid it. The hitch now leaves both FSMs as it sets them, as the game's own attachables
  do.

## Install

Unzip into `Apocalypter/BepInEx/plugins`, replacing the `BurnersUtilities` folder.

latest.title: Engine Sim 1.8.1
latest.notes:
# Engine Sim 1.8.1

## Fixes

- **The starter moves the car in gear on a worn-out engine again.** An engine whose table gives no `peak_torque`
  (one from another mod's table, such as SigmaMod's Astron) kept the game's clutch, which the game sizes from its
  power figure; at 0 % condition that is 1 kW, and the clutch slipped under the starter. Such an engine now has its
  peak torque measured once by a dyno pull in the background, and its clutch sized from it like any other. The log
  gives the figure to put in its table.
- The FSM dump (`Debug.VerboseLog`) no longer fills Unity's log with errors from menu FSMs that haven't started.

## Install

Unzip into `Apocalypter/BepInEx/plugins`, replacing the `EngineSim` folder.

latest.title: Ultimate Tools 2.3.7 — Held-item drop fix and suspension damping
latest.notes:
Ultimate Tools 2.3.7 fixes held items disappearing when putting the tool away and adds progressive damping for raised suspension to address shaking at high ride heights.

Pressing X now drops a held item at its current position before putting away the wrench or screwdriver. The native drop sequence restores collisions, gravity and inherited vehicle velocity. Rotation and scroll movement are covered, and empty hands leave nearby items alone. Using a toolbox to put the tool away follows the same drop behavior.

Each axle's bump and rebound damping decrease linearly from 100% of the native lift-kit rates at zero added height to 25% at +15 cm. Intermediate examples: +5 cm retains 75%, +10 cm retains 50%. Front/rear balance is included separately for each axle. Lowering retains native damping. Width alone does not change damping.

Rates are calculated from the original per-wheel values, so repeated adjustments do not compound the reduction. Reset, kit removal, global disable and component shutdown restore values still controlled by Ultimate Tools. Native stock/lifted transitions establish fresh baselines; external damping edits are respected. Existing saved height and balance require no migration. Spring strength, travel and center of mass remain native.

Installation: extract UltimateTools-2.3.7.zip into BepInEx/plugins, replacing the existing UltimateTools folder, then restart. Disable DukeDamperTrial when testing to avoid compounding damping reductions.

Validation: Release build passed with zero warnings and errors. All five offline suites passed, including 179 progressive damping checks. All 20 focused native Unity checks passed against actual NWH components, covering the curve, axle balance, repeated updates, reset, kit removal/refit, disable/re-enable, external edits, replacement dampers, stock transition and unchanged spring/curve settings. Verification ran in an isolated local game runtime without opening a player save. Actual driving and high-lift shake reduction still need player testing.

Put-away validation: 110 focused native Unity checks passed for both toolboxes, held/rotate/scroll states, stale controller caches, native release events, restored physics and world pose, release ordering, empty hands and hovered items. The full native regression suite passed all 2,330 checks.

latest.title: Wild Wasteland 1.0.4
latest.notes:
# Wild Wasteland 1.0.4 — Save reliability

Saves now wait for pending terrain generation and application to finish before writing, then hold terrain streaming until save publication completes. Pausing game time alone did not stop MapMagic.Update: moving locations during serialization tripped the consistency guard and subsequently disabled saving. This affected standard WW and WWMP independently of Towns. The guard remains; the race is prevented at the save boundary.

Location discovery saves and journal publication now use a same-directory Windows replacement rename instead of Mono File.Replace, which failed with Win32 error 1175 in the supplied player log. Verified staging and journal rollback remain in place. Save controls stay visible, with their existing availability/status checks, rather than disappearing after a failure. Preparation cancellation/timeout releases input, time and streaming without starting a write transaction; actual write failures still report their error and retain consistency protection. New named saves remain separate files; only explicit overwrite targets an existing named save.

No new settings, save identities or formats. Two Core prefixes run a boolean check outside saves; pending terrain drains under the existing native application budget. Restores the accepted camp/building icons in the runtime package so updating no longer replaces them with older artwork. No personal configs or saves are modified or bundled. Unrelated pending wiki work is excluded.

latest.title: Wild Wasteland MP RC11 (0.1.47)
latest.notes:
# Wild Wasteland MP RC11 (0.1.47) — Client crossbow tooltip

Fixes a client seeing **20 damage** when hovering over a crossbow while the host sees **50**. Apocalypter Multiplayer adds `MP_` to replicated item names; the tooltip's crossbow name check now recognizes that prefix. Applies to both ordinary hover text and the shop Buy tooltip.

This corrects the displayed number. The existing projectile calculation already recognizes replicated crossbows and applies the same 2.5× base-damage multiplier. Projectile damage, settings and save formats are unchanged. The tooltip correction remains conditional on Guns projectiles and player projectiles being enabled; disabling those retains vanilla text.

Includes the RC10 purchase-sync, occupant collision protection and autosave-warning fixes. Update and restart every peer with matching builds; handshake 24 remains. Extract the full ZIP into `BepInEx/plugins`, keeping standard Wild Wasteland disabled. Multiplayer requires separately installed **BepInEx 5 x64** and [Apocalypter Multiplayer 0.4.1](https://www.nexusmods.com/apocalypter/mods/10). No dependency DLLs are bundled.

Manual check: host and guest hover the same ordinary crossbow and an unpaid shop crossbow with player projectiles enabled; both should show 50. Repeat after purchase/drop and reconnect, and check another weapon's tooltip remains unchanged. With player projectiles disabled, confirm vanilla crossbow text remains 20. Runtime/visual acceptance remains **Testing**; no game or harness was launched.

Source: `src/Modules/Guns/WeaponDamageText.cs` now checks the crossbow name immediately after an optional native `MP_` prefix, preserving case-insensitive matching, literal text checks and finalizer restoration. No new patch target, hook, job, packet or config key.

Windows Release/Deploy=false passed with zero warnings/errors. Exact stage `V:/Repos/Apocalypter/_releases/WildWastelandMP_0.1.47-RC11a.dll`, built/staged DLL MD5 **F7B44D8615C47F652869847749272DE9**. Current standard-WW installation/running game retained; no MP folder/dependency, no deployment or live config/save edits.

Runtime-only ZIP: 287 files, 236,668,234 bytes; SHA256 **f6cd3b783238b2b32ec022e3847a86902651ab3815ae7c0d424119016791b774**. CRC, exact source bytes, safe unique paths, single plugin DLL, 18 loading images and 156 retained baseline assets checked. Dependency DLLs, documentation and personal runtime data are excluded.

mods.name: Women of Wasteland
mods.author: DeonUrist
mods.summary: Turns a share of Flexa and Sprokka raiders into female Gungirls and Shootas with their own models, textures and voices. Part of what was Apocaraider.
mods.deprecatedReason: Women of Wasteland is included in Wild Wasteland 1.0. Install Wild Wasteland and disable this standalone plugin to avoid duplicate features. Keep existing configuration and data files for migration.

latest.title: WomenOfWasteland 1.0.0
latest.notes:
First standalone release. Female raiders in the wasteland: female models and textures, their own voice lines, female corpses, and the appearance saved with the game. Ships its Models and Sounds folders next to the DLL.

Part of the Apocaraider split: **Gunplay**, **GunplayHUD**, **NPCAI** and **WomenOfWasteland** replace the combined Apocaraider (now frozen). Each works on its own and with any combination of the others. **Remove Apocaraider** when installing these, otherwise its hooks run twice. Old Apocaraider settings are imported on first run.

**Install:** unzip into `BepInEx\plugins` (creates `BepInEx\plugins\WomenOfWasteland\`).
